### Findings
Across authorized product scope enforced at execution, completed items (`order_items.status = 'Complete'`) were aggregated at the item grain by product department with no date filter applied [q1]. Default revenue is defined as `SUM(sale_price)` for completed items.

| department | complete_revenue | complete_items |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Men | 70.0 | 7 |
| Women | 140.0 | 7 |

- Both departments have an identical count of 7 completed items [q1].
- Complete-item revenue for Women (140.0) is double that of Men (70.0) [q1].

### Limitations
- The query did not apply a date filter or return timestamps, so completeness and distribution across historical time periods were not measured [q1].
- The metric reflects item-level completed sales revenue and item counts, not distinct orders, distinct customers, or product costs [q1].

### Action items (proposed)
- What is the breakdown of completed item revenue and item volume by department when grouped by order creation year or month?
- How many distinct orders (`COUNT(DISTINCT order_key)`) and distinct customers (`COUNT(DISTINCT customer_key)`) account for the completed sales in each department?
